mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales of 2% or more over the past quarter indicates weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS QoQ < -2% does not correlate with subsequent earnings declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE MoM > 0.5pp does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO MoM < -1% does not correlate with subsequent supply chain disruptions.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS > 5% and rising does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling housing starts (HOUST) signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of UNRATE > 5% and HOUST MoM < -5% does not correlate with subsequent economic contractions.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which typically lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances with PAYEMS increase > 300,000, or PAYEMS increase > 300,000 does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending increases.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and stable, it signals accommodative monetary policy that supports economic growth and increases corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS < 2% and stable does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.
